Apple updated the privacy policy of the Apple Store app to include provisions related to an upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Details are as follows.

Apple is expanding the application of AI in retail

According to MacRumors, a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant" has now been added to the Apple Store app and its privacy page, with the following content:

In other words, the Apple Store app may introduce a chatbot in the future that provides personalised responses based on user data to help users make purchasing decisions.

Apple stated that before sharing chat content with anonymous partners that provide assistant responses, it will first remove personally identifiable information, suggesting that some of the experience will likely be powered by third-party models.

Chat records will be kept within the app for users to review at any time, and Apple will also retain them for business analytics purposes. Users can independently choose whether to allow conversation content to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant through the newly added "Chat Improvements" setting.

The wording in Apple's privacy policy indicates that the virtual assistant will initially launch in selected countries or regions, most likely debuting in English-speaking markets before gradually expanding to more languages and regions.

This announcement comes months after Apple added an AI chatbot to its Sales Coach app, which provides sales and technical resources for Apple retail partners. Users can access the chatbot through the "Ask" tab, which answers questions based on Apple's official training materials and documentation.

In addition, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" at select retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe, and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing employees to focus on assisting customers without being distracted by taking notes.

To learn more about the Apple Store app and privacy, please click here.
